deep.reconstruction:
This page belongs to the motivational introduction of Grothendieck's November–December 1967 IHES lectures on crystals, published as 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (notes by J. Coates and O. Jussila) in Dix exposés sur la cohomologie des schémas, 1968.

The argument continues from p.11. ℓ-adic cohomology (ℓ ≠ p) cannot see p-torsion phenomena in characteristic p. Even if a 'concrete' integrality question (for example, whether certain coefficients are rational) is answered positively, one only gets integrality away from p, i.e. numbers of the form n/p^s.

This page states the consequence: without a p-adic theory one does not understand cohomological p-torsion in characteristic p. The p-primary part gets 'mutilated' in statements. The example is Tate's Bourbaki exposé (Séminaire Bourbaki 306, 1966, on the Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture and its geometric analogue). There the p-part of the Artin–Tate formula for the order of the Brauer group of a surface over a finite field could only be justified heuristically. The marginal note seems to say the same: p-torsion in the Brauer group of a surface needs a p-adic theory.

One would therefore want functors X ↦ H^i(X), from smooth projective varieties over k to finitely generated Z_p-modules or to Q_p-vector spaces. These should have the usual properties: Künneth, duality, correct Betti numbers.

An argument of Serre shows that no such functor exists, already for H^1 and low-dimensional varieties. Serre's argument is formulated with Q_p coefficients. A supersingular elliptic curve E over F_{p^2}, or over an algebraically closed field, has endomorphism algebra End(E)⊗Q equal to the quaternion algebra ramified at p and ∞. If H^1(E) were a 2-dimensional Q_p-vector space, this algebra would act faithfully on it. That would force the quaternion algebra to split over Q_p, which it does not.

Conclusion, continued on p.13: the natural coefficient ring is W(k), the Witt vectors of a perfect field k, with fraction field K = W(k)[1/p], which contains Q_p. This is the programme that crystalline cohomology later realised (Grothendieck 1966–68, Berthelot 1974).
errors: No mathematical error. The scope of Serre's argument is slightly mis-stated: it needs only H^1 of curves (supersingular elliptic curves), and it rules out Q_p (hence Z_p) coefficients only when k contains F_{p^2}, or more generally when the quaternion endomorphisms are defined over k. The page's restriction to 'VA de dim ≤ 2' (reading uncertain) is therefore more than needed.

deep.surprise_reason: This is lecture-preparation motivation that matches the published introduction of the 1967 crystals lectures almost exactly (Serre's argument, W(k) coefficients, the p-part of the Brauer group). Nothing here is new.
transcription_corrections: 'modules de t.f.' = modules de type fini.
'Des [désastres] mutilations ne manquent' — likely 'Des mutilations ne manquent pas [d'apparaître]' in the context of statements in characteristic p; the struck word is unclear.
The 'formule pour 2[?]' is probably 'formule pour p' or 'pour le p-primaire', referring to the p-part of Tate's Brauer-group formula.
'aux VA de dim ≤ 2' — the numeral is uncertain; mathematically Serre's argument needs only dimension 1 (curves).
